scenario.title: Faraday Development Ltd v West Berkshire Council
scenario.description: West Berkshire Council entered into a development agreement with St Modwen Developments Ltd for approximately £125 million, structured as a conditional land agreement. Faraday Development Ltd challenged the arrangement, alleging that it was in substance a public works contract that should have been competitively procured under the Public Contracts Regulations. The High Court initially dismissed the claim, but the Court of Appeal reversed this decision, holding that the agreement was indeed a public works contract and declaring its ineffectiveness.

interests: Compliance & Legality: Uphold the lawfulness and procedural correctness of our procurement process.
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid significant delay costs associated with re-running this £125,000,000 contract.
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Ensure timely delivery of a major development project that impacts local infrastructure and services.
Reputation & Public Accountability: Maintain public confidence in our procurement practices and avoid adverse media scrutiny.
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our original evaluation and award, which was made in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations and the Procurement Act 2023.

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: £125,000,000 contract value at stake
Fairness & Transparency: Dispute over whether agreement was competitively procured
Protection of Reputation: Bid team's performance and credibility on the line
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids or competition to be re-run
Award of damages for any financial losses incurred due to the ineffectiveness of the agreement
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: Request West Berkshire Council reconsider their evaluation process and provide detailed feedback on why they deemed St Modwen Developments Ltd's bid the most suitable

messages.message: Faraday Development Ltd's claim that our development agreement with St Modwen Developments Ltd is in substance a public works contract requires clarification. Can you specify which particular aspects of the agreement led the Court of Appeal to this conclusion? We are willing to provide additional transparency regarding our evaluation process, but we must ensure that any disclosure does not compromise the integrity of our procurement decision.

We appreciate your willingness to provide additional transparency regarding our evaluation process. However, we would like to clarify that our previous statement was not about the specifics of the development agreement with St Modwen Developments Ltd, but rather about the perceived injustice and potential for financial or commercial gain in relation to our bid. We believe that certain aspects of the evaluation process were inconsistent and may have impacted our chances of winning the contract. Can you provide more information on how you evaluated our bid, particularly with regards to the scoring discrepancies we've pointed out?

We acknowledge Faraday Development Ltd's concerns regarding scoring discrepancies in their bid evaluation. To address these concerns, we are willing to provide a detailed breakdown of our evaluation process, including the specific criteria used for each scoring category and the scores awarded to each bidder. We will also review our records to identify any potential manifest errors that may have impacted Faraday Development Ltd's chances of winning the contract. However, we must emphasize that our evaluation was conducted in accordance with the published evaluation criteria and that any disclosure must be balanced against the need to protect commercial confidentiality.
messages.concession_made: A voluntary standstill extension for engagement to discuss potential manifest errors

messages.message: We appreciate your willingness to provide a detailed breakdown of your evaluation process and review potential manifest errors that may have impacted our chances of winning the contract. However, we would like to request that you also provide any supporting documentation or records related to the scoring discrepancies we've pointed out, such as evaluator comments, scoring sheets, or other relevant materials. This will help us better understand how these discrepancies were identified and addressed during the evaluation process. Furthermore, we would like to propose a joint review of our bid with your team to identify any areas where we may have misunderstood or misinterpreted the evaluation criteria.
messages.proposal: A joint review of our bid with your team

messages.message: We appreciate Faraday Development Ltd's willingness to engage in a joint review of their bid with our team. We agree that this would be a valuable exercise in ensuring transparency and accuracy in our evaluation process. However, we must ensure that any such review is conducted in a way that maintains the integrity of our procurement decision and does not compromise commercial confidentiality. To facilitate this, we propose that the joint review be limited to specific scoring categories where discrepancies have been identified, and that all discussions and findings be documented and shared with both parties. We are also willing to provide additional training to our evaluation team on the importance of accurate and consistent scoring in future procurements.
messages.proposal: Joint Review of Specific Scoring Categories

messages.message: We appreciate your willingness to provide additional transparency and review potential manifest errors that may have impacted our chances of winning the contract. We agree that a joint review is a valuable exercise in ensuring transparency and accuracy in your evaluation process. However, we would like to propose that the joint review be conducted by an independent third-party expert who can provide an objective assessment of our bid and identify any areas where we may have misunderstood or misinterpreted the evaluation criteria. This will help ensure that the review is conducted in a way that maintains the integrity of your procurement decision and does not compromise commercial confidentiality.
messages.proposal: An independent third-party expert to conduct the joint review

messages.message: We are willing to accept your proposal for an independent third-party expert to conduct a joint review of Faraday Development Ltd's bid, provided that this expert is agreed upon by both parties and that their report is made available to us. We also propose that the joint review be conducted in accordance with the principles outlined in the Procurement Act 2023, specifically section 12(1), which requires that public procurement decisions be taken in a transparent and proportionate manner.
messages.proposal: Independent third-party expert-led joint review of Faraday Development Ltd's bid
messages.concession_made: Additional transparency regarding our evaluation process

messages.message: We appreciate your willingness to accept our proposal for an independent third-party expert to conduct a joint review of our bid. We are willing to propose that this expert be appointed through a transparent and competitive process, with both parties having equal input in selecting the most suitable candidate. This will ensure that the review is conducted impartially and with integrity. Additionally, we would like to request that the Contracting Authority provide us with a detailed timeline for the joint review process, including milestones and deadlines for submission of reports and findings.
messages.proposal: The independent third-party expert be appointed through a transparent and competitive process

However, I note that the parties' positions suggest a potential issue with transparency and consistency in the evaluation process.

This scenario is qualitative, as it involves a dispute over the classification of a development agreement and whether it should have been competitively procured. I will assess compliance qualitatively instead of computing a numeric score. The Contracting Authority's proposal for an independent third-party expert to conduct a joint review is a reasonable step towards transparency and proportionality. However, the Aggrieved Bidder's request for a detailed timeline and milestones may be seen as an attempt to micromanage the process. Nevertheless, this does not necessarily indicate a manifest error in the Contracting Authority's process. The key issue here is whether the development agreement was indeed a public works contract that should have been competitively procured. The Court of Appeal has already declared its ineffectiveness, suggesting that there may be grounds for the Aggrieved Bidder's challenge.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome is more favorable than our BATNA (defending in TCC court, which would cost £50k+ and take 6-12 months) as we were able to avoid the costs and risks associated with litigation.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We have successfully negotiated a re-evaluation of the development agreement that addresses Faraday Development Ltd's concerns regarding scoring discrepancies in their bid evaluation. The joint review process will provide transparency and accuracy in our evaluation process, while also maintaining the integrity of our procurement decision.
what_was_achieved: Provided a detailed breakdown of our evaluation process to address scoring discrepancies
Agreed to a joint review of Faraday Development Ltd's bid with an independent third-party expert
Proposed additional training for our evaluation team on accurate and consistent scoring
what_was_conceded: Providing supporting documentation or records related to the scoring discrepancies
Limiting the scope of the joint review to specific scoring categories where discrepancies have been identified

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The negotiation outcome is more favorable than our BATNA (pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings), as we have achieved some level of transparency and accountability in the evaluation process, which may help us understand how to improve for future bids. However, the outcome falls short of a complete resolution, as we did not achieve a reversal of the Court's decision declaring the agreement ineffectiveness.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated an independent third-party expert review of our bid, which will provide a more objective assessment of our chances of winning the contract and help identify areas for improvement. Additionally, the Contracting Authority has agreed to provide additional transparency regarding their evaluation process and review potential manifest errors that may have impacted our chances.

Increased transparency in the evaluation process
Potential review of manifest errors that may have impacted our chances
what_was_conceded: No reversal of the Court's decision declaring the agreement ineffectiveness
Limited scope for the joint review, focusing on specific scoring categories only
No guarantee of a favorable outcome from the independent third-party expert review

key_sticking_points: Classification of the development agreement between Faraday Development Ltd and St Modwen Developments Ltd
Potential manifest errors in the evaluation process that may have impacted the Aggrieved Bidder's chances of winning the contract
Transparency and consistency in the evaluation process
